_readme: What changed in each version of the app, written for players. The app shows the entries between the installed version and the update it offers (fetched from main, so a version that is already out can read the notes of the next one), and once after an update.

One entry per released version, newest first. Each item: kind (new, improved, fixed), area (a short word: Meter, Reports, History...), title (one line), text (what it does, in plain words) and, when it helps, example (a short real situation, with made-up player names).
The release workflow puts the same items in the GitHub release notes (Tools/changelog/release-notes.mjs).

items.title: Your Combat Power matches the game right away
items.text: The meter took your own Combat Power from the legion list the game sends when you log in, so after an enchant or a new piece it kept the old number until you logged in again. The game also sends your Combat Power every time it changes, failed enchants included; the meter now reads that, so the bar, your line, the group list and the character window show the new number within seconds. The same goes for your Item Level.
items.example: Enchant your weapon from +18 to +19: the bar shows the new CP at once, no relog needed.

items.title: Your gear updates as you change it
items.text: The character window showed your equipment as the game listed it when you logged in or changed servers. The game sends a piece again whenever you enchant it, roll its stats again or put it on, and the window now takes each of those as it happens: enchant level, stones and stats. It also shows your Item Level and Combat Power as the game counts them.
items.example: Rolling the stats of an earring again and again? The window shows every new roll.

items.title: Your own Combat Power in the fights you upload
items.text: The website's logs knew your Combat Power only from its own records, often an older number. The fights you upload now carry your number at the time of the fight, like everyone else's, so the Class Stats by Combat Power count you where you belong.

items.title: Links only ever open as web pages
items.text: Every link the app opens in your browser (player and fight pages, the news, legion invites, your fight history) is checked once more right before it opens: only a normal https web page goes through. Windows opens whatever it is handed, a program or a shared folder too, so anything else is simply not opened. The links were already checked where the app gets them; this is a second lock.

items.title: The game's pictures can't fill your disk
items.text: The pack of game pictures the app downloads is measured while it unpacks: at most 8 MB a picture, 512 MB and 50,000 pictures in all, and the download stops if more arrives than the website announced. A pack over that stops, and nothing of it is kept. Today's pack is about 5,000 pictures and 40 MB, well inside the limits.

items.title: The Abyss radar stays out of dungeons, also when the meter missed the way in
items.text: The radar, the enemy card and the death recap already stayed out of dungeons and raids, by the zone the game names when you enter. When the meter didn't catch that moment (it was started or updated inside, or the game changed servers too fast), it still thought you were outside, and the radar could come up in Exploration, Conquest or Ludra. Now the monsters around tell it too: a dungeon's boss, or its monsters where they stand only in that dungeon. And a member of your own group is never taken for an enemy.
items.example: Updated the meter in the middle of a Fire Temple run? The radar no longer pops up at Black Smoke Murute.

items.title: Untick a genus and its Black Cloud pets follow
items.text: On the Pets page, unticking a genus for the alerts (Fera, Varian ...) now also unticks that genus's pets in the Black Cloud Merchant list; ticking it again ticks back the ones a character still needs. Ticking one pet of a genus that is off turns the genus back on for it.
items.example: Don't care about Fera pets? Untick Fera once instead of every Fera pet in the list.

items.title: Full size for the app and its windows
items.text: The app and its windows (Timers, the pages opened in a window of their own, History ...) have a full size button beside minimise, and a double click on the title bar does the same. Full size keeps the taskbar in sight.
items.example: Open the Timers window, press the square beside the minus: it fills the screen.

items.title: Timers and world bosses can step aside in dungeons
items.text: The timers overlay and the world boss overlay each have a new switch, "Hide in dungeons and raids" (on the Timers page and the World bosses page). With it on, they disappear when you enter a dungeon or raid and come back when you leave. Off by default, so nothing changes until you switch it on.
items.example: Running Fire Temple? The event countdowns and the boss list stay out of your way.

items.title: Leave maxed pets out of the pet information
items.text: The pet information at the monster has a new switch, "Leave out pets already at their top level" (Pets page). With it on, a pet your character has maxed is no longer listed, so only the ones still worth farming show.
items.example: Intermediate Fire Spirit at Level 3 (max) no longer shows up while you farm Fire Temple.

items.title: Signing in with Discord finishes even when its window was closed
items.text: Signing the app in happens in the browser: Connect Discord (Discord asks for your password there when the browser isn't signed in to Discord, even if the Discord app is), Authorize, then Approve. The app noticed the approval only while its sign-in window stayed open, so a closed window left the app signed out. It now keeps waiting by itself, and its window comes back to say who it is signed in as. The page in the browser now says each step, why a Discord sign-in didn't come back (it took too long, was cancelled on Discord's page), and keeps the code even when Discord's login finishes in another tab. A sign-in now has 30 minutes instead of 15.
items.example: Sign in with Discord, close the window, log in to Discord in the browser, Authorize, Approve: the app pops its account window up with "Signed in as …".

items.title: Map, Legion and Streaming no longer vanish without a word
items.text: When the privacy policy was declined (at the first start, for example), the app runs in its restricted mode, and the Map with the Cube finder, Legion and Streaming were simply gone from the column, while some links to them did nothing. They now stay in the column with a padlock: they open a page that says why they are off, with the privacy policy to read again. Home says it too. Accepting brings them back at once, without a restart, and declining in the first-start setup now takes them away at once too.
items.example: A friend without a Map tab: the Map entry shows a padlock, a click on it explains it, and "Show the privacy policy" turns it back on.

items.title: The right icons for the Cleric's skills
items.text: Several Cleric skills showed the wrong icon in the skill list, the meter's breakdown and the overlays: Benevolence had another skill's, and Salvation, Power Burst, Absolution, Voice of Doom, Prayer of Amplification, Noble Aura and some passives each showed the one of the skill next to them. They all show their own icon now, as in the game. The same was fixed for a few Gladiator, Templar, Ranger, Sorcerer and Chanter skills, and skills that had no icon at all, like Comrade in Arms and Defiance, have one now.
items.example: Benevolence shows its own golden circle now, and Noble Aura is no longer a copy of Prayer of Amplification.

items.title: Switch off the grey or the green part of the bars
items.text: The grey part of a meter bar (what a player's buffs gave the others) and the green part with its + healing figure (their healing on the others) each have their own switch now, in Meter look under Bars. Switch off one and the other stays; switch off both for bars of the own damage alone. Without the grey part the rDPS view draws the whole rDPS in the class colour, so the bars still follow the order.
items.example: Only want to see who did the damage? Switch off "Buffs on the bar" and "Healing on the bar": no grey, no green, no +12.4K.

items.title: The whole party in your group's list
items.text: A full party showed three players in the group list: everyone but you. You are on it now too, marked "you", in Combat Power order with the others.

items.title: Only this map's own pets, for a rift
items.text: A new switch on the Pet map page shows only the pets you can get on the map you are on and on no other open map. The map, the list and the route all follow it: what to farm while a rift into the other side's land is open.

items.title: Says when pet levels are from your last login
items.text: When the app starts while you are already in the game, it uses the pet levels it saved at your last login until the game sends its list again at the next map change. A pet you finished in between could still show as level 1, and the route could send you to it. The pet list and the pet info over a monster now say so: change map or teleport once and the levels are up to date.

items.title: How the kill went against your best
items.text: When a boss dies, the boss line on the meter now shows how long the kill took and your DPS against your best kill of that boss before it: green with "new best" when you beat it, or "first kill" the first time. It stays until the next pull or for three minutes.
items.example: Killed Watchdog Kwapo in 1:05 · ▲ 12% vs your best 26.8k · new best 30.0k

items.title: Your group's list folds away in the dungeon
items.text: The list of your group that opens by itself while you get a group together now goes away when you enter the dungeon or raid, and doesn't open again by itself inside. You can still open Find a player yourself any time.

items.title: Crowded world bosses upload again
items.text: A world boss with more than 64 players was refused whole by atreia.app. The upload now takes you and the 63 players with the most damage, like any other fight.

items.title: A proper setup wizard
items.text: The installer is now a setup wizard: it says what the app does and needs before it installs, offers to open the Npcap download page when Npcap is missing, and can start the app at the end. The app installs and updates exactly as before.
items.example: New players see what Atreia is before anything is installed, instead of a quick splash.

items.title: Closing an overlay's settings no longer closes the app
items.text: Closing the settings that an overlay's gear opens could close the whole app (it happened most with the Abyss radar). It closes cleanly now, by its X, by Esc or by clicking somewhere else.

items.title: The PvP overlays stay out of dungeons and raids
items.text: The enemy card, the Abyss radar and the death recap no longer come up in dungeons and raids. They still work in the Abyss, the open world and the arenas.

items.title: Skills on your skill bar no longer vanish from the cooldowns
items.text: Some skills, like Focused Block, disappeared from the cooldowns after their first use and left a hole among your tiles. A skill on your skill bar now stays where you put it. Only basic attacks and chain skills are left out, and you can still hide any skill yourself in the Skill Assist.

items.title: Every overlay has its own settings button and padlock
items.text: Rest the mouse on an overlay in the game and a small gear and a padlock show in its top right corner. The padlock locks or frees it right there: free, drag it anywhere and pull its edges; locked, clicks go through to the game again. The gear opens its settings beside it: its size, how see-through its background is, locked or not, back to its first place, turn it off, or all its settings in the app. No need to open the app to change an overlay any more.
items.example: The timers sit too big over your minimap: hover them, click the gear, slide Size to 80 % and click back into the game.

items.title: Monster pictures on Grind and Loot
items.text: The best monsters to farm, the loot by monster and the drop rates now show each monster's picture next to its name.

items.title: Pet pictures on the pet list and over the monster
items.text: The pet list overlay shows each pet's picture framed in its colour on the map (collectibles show theirs too), and the pet information over a monster shows the pet's picture before its level.

items.title: A tidier world boss overlay
items.text: A boss whose time isn't known yet shows a quiet dash instead of the same sentence on every line, with one note under the list saying to visit its map once.

items.title: The replay on the website shows the boss and its attacks
items.text: A fight's replay on its page now shows the boss itself standing on the floor, turned the way it faces, and every attack as you'd see it coming: its shape on the floor (circle, ring, cone, line, cross or the whole room) filling up as the boss winds it up and flashing red when it lands, the pools it leaves, and a ring on whoever got caught. The app sends the attacks with the positions from this version on; fights uploaded before show the boss and which way it faces.

versions.headline: The Abyss radar becomes a round war map, and the PvP overlays show in the Abyss

items.title: The radar is a map of everyone around you
items.text: Every player in view sits on a disc around you, north up, 50 m to the edge: enemies in red with a haze where they gather and the strongest one named, your party in blue, your legion in violet and the rest of your faction in green. Under it you see who has the numbers within 25 m, your kills, assists and deaths in this zone, and the three strongest enemies with their Combat Power against yours.
items.example: "Outnumbered · 4 v 11 within 25 m" as a group comes over the ridge, Kraeger named in red at its front.

items.title: The enemy card, the radar and the death recap show in the Abyss
items.text: Many enemies in the Abyss came with no server, so they weren't taken for enemies; anyone who trades hits with you now counts as one. The app also mistook the Abyss's own bars for an open game window and hid the overlays during fights. If one still doesn't show, pvp-log.txt beside your settings says why.

items.title: Solid backgrounds for the PvP overlays
items.text: The enemy card, the radar and the death recap no longer let the game show through. Each overlay's own opacity setting still changes it.

items.title: The Characters page as it was
items.text: Your characters are a column on the left again, and All characters is the table it was, with the season missions and the inventory under it. Each character's own page keeps what 2.0 gave it: all your Odyle Energy together at the top, cards that fold and stay folded, and warnings that say what you'd lose and when.

items.title: The wipe review says what it shows
items.text: It now reads Wipe review, names the boss and the health it was left at, labels its columns (who died, in order, when, and what killed them), and tells the whole story when you point at a name.
items.example: Ultimate Berk was left at 31% health · Draegor died 2:14 into the try: Searing Breath (12,400).

versions.headline: Atreia App 2.0 (beta): crafting, Grind, Abyss tools and all your characters on one board. The new tools are still in beta, so tell us in the Atreia Discord what breaks

items.title: Your pace against your best
items.text: During a boss fight, a line under the boss's health shows your DPS against your best kill of that boss on this character: ▲ green when you're ahead, ▼ when you're behind.
items.example: ▲ 6% vs your best 41.6K on Transcendent Bakarma, a minute in.

items.title: How far each try got
items.text: Wipe and pull again: the meter shows which try this is, the lowest the boss's health got in any try, and where the last one left it, so you can see the group getting closer. It counts the tries of the last few hours since that boss's last kill.
items.example: Try 4 · best 18% · last 31%

items.title: Buffs show a preview while you place them
items.text: In the overlay editor the buffs overlay shows a few sample buffs when none are on your character, so you can see how it will look. The other overlays already show samples while you place them.

items.title: A new crafting page that knows where everything is
items.text: The crafting calculator is rebuilt. It counts your bag, your storage, the server storage and what your other characters on the server hold unbound, and each material shows where it lies. It also counts when the app started after you logged in: each character's items are kept from its last login. Every place can be switched off with one click at the top.
items.example: 90 ore needed: 40 in the bag, 25 in storage and 18 on your alt Arkhel. 7 left to get, 2.1K Kinah at the market.

items.title: Market prices for your server
items.text: Every material and every product shows its market price for your server: what each recipe is worth, what its materials cost, the profit, and what buying the missing materials would cost.

items.title: What you can craft right now
items.text: A tab lists every recipe your items already cover, how many times you can craft it, and what you'd make on each one at market prices, the most profitable first. One click adds it to your plan. You can also search every recipe by its name or one of its materials.

items.title: A clearer crafting overlay
items.text: The overlay over the game shows how far your plan is, each recipe with a bar, what is still missing, what buying it costs, and where the part you have is lying when it isn't in your bag.

items.title: Grind: Kinah and Abyss Points per hour
items.text: Switch the meter to Grind (next to Stagger) while you farm. It shows how much Kinah and how many Abyss Points you're making an hour, in big, with your kills and the loot you picked up and what it's worth at the market. The hourly numbers are your session's average: a big kill lifts them right away, then they settle as the minutes go by. Breaks of more than five minutes don't count against you.
items.example: 34 minutes in Chaotic Middle Reshanta: 1.25M Kinah an hour, 32.8K Abyss Points an hour, 376 kills an hour.

items.title: The Loot tool is now Grind
items.text: The tool shows your grind going on and your earlier sessions side by side, so you can compare maps and characters. The loot log you know is still there, as the second tab.

items.title: Enemy card
items.text: Tab onto an enemy player and a card shows their class, level, server, legion, Combat Power and item level, and how their Combat Power compares with yours. If the game didn't send their numbers (for example the app started while they were already nearby), the card looks them up from their character page. Place it where you like in the overlay editor; it only shows while an enemy is selected. On the Overlays page you can have it show players of your own side too.

items.title: Enemy radar
items.text: A small list over the game of every enemy player around you, the strongest first, with their class and Combat Power against yours. When someone at least 20% stronger than you shows up, they appear in red at the top for a few seconds, so you can back off before they reach you. Numbers the game didn't send are looked up, like on the enemy card. It only shows while enemies are in view.
items.example: Kaelith (Gladiator) 412K, 38% stronger than you, just came into view.

items.title: Death recap
items.text: When you die, a card shows what killed you: the last 15 seconds of damage you took, by player and skill, the blow that finished you, and the healing you got in that time. It stays for 30 seconds, then clears itself.

items.title: Rivals
items.text: The app remembers the enemy players you fight: how often you met, how many times you killed them and how many times they killed you. The record shows on their enemy card and on the radar the next time you run into them.
items.example: Vorrin: fought 6×, 4 kills, 2 deaths.

items.title: The best monsters to farm
items.text: The Grind tool ranks the monsters you've killed at least five times by what each kill brings you on average: its Kinah plus the market value of its drops on your server, with the Abyss Points next to it. So you know which pack actually pays.

items.title: Kills count even without a drop
items.text: Grind and Loot used to count a kill only when you picked something up from it. Every monster you take down counts now, so the kills an hour and the averages per monster are right.

items.title: Wipe review
items.text: After a try that ends without the kill, the meter shows who died first and when, what killed each of them, the skill that took down the most of the group, and how much health the boss had left against your best try of the last hours. It goes away by itself after a few minutes or when you pull again.
items.example: Try 4: Lyra died first at 1:42 to Shadow Burst. The boss was at 18%, your best try today got it to 9%.

items.title: Share cards for Discord
items.text: One click turns a fight into a clean picture, ready to paste into Discord with Ctrl+V: right-click a fight in History, pick it from the meter's menu, or press Share on a grind session. The picture is also kept in your Pictures folder, under Atreia App.

items.title: Every character on one board
items.text: All characters shows every counter as a row and every character as a column, so you see at a glance which alt has what: Odyle Energy (with all of it together and how many runs it makes), the daily tasks, Nightmare and the daily dungeons, the keys your server's characters share, this week's Ascension Trial, Subjugation, Ludra's Abyssal Forge with its boss, the Conquest and Transcendence rewards and the Abyss Corridors. Only what the Global servers have is listed. A counter turns red when it's so full that part of the next refill is lost, and amber when the week's tickets are about to reset unused. Sections fold and stay folded. Eight characters fit side by side. Season missions and the inventory have tabs of their own.
items.example: Kaivhan's Nightmare is at 13/14 with +2 coming at 08:00: the cell is red and says −1 at 08:00.

items.title: A clearer page for each character
items.text: The Odyle Energy card shows all your energy together at the top (basic, charged and in items) and how many runs it makes. Every other row is shaded, the two small daily dungeons say they're daily dungeons, warnings say exactly what you'd lose and when, and every card folds and stays folded. Characters are picked from a bar at the top.

items.title: Pick any character, dates in the app's language
items.text: Journey shows your characters as chips under the title, in the app and over the game, and every character the meter knows can be picked. Days and months are named in the app's language, and the columns of your days line up on every PC.

items.title: Everyone's Combat Power in your group at once
items.text: The game's group finder tells each member's Combat Power and Item Level, so the meter now shows them on your group's rows the moment someone joins, without waiting for the website. The list is sorted strongest first, in Ludra, Conquest, exploration and any other group, and so is the list of players fighting with you.
items.example: You join a Conquest room: Torvan 194,214, Lysse 175,232 and Oriel 171,271 show up top to bottom before anyone has said a word.

items.title: A settings button over the game
items.text: The Atreia button is now a small settings button with the overlay editor's keys above it. A click opens the overlay menu. It no longer moves when you drag it, which was laggy: move it and size it in the overlay editor, with Windows' own smooth move like every other overlay. Its menu keeps a sensible size when you make the button bigger or smaller.

items.title: No more jumping while you drag
items.text: "Place overlays on a grid" made every overlay jump in 20 px steps while dragged, which felt like lag. It's off now, and the overlay editor has its own Snap to the grid switch. When it's on, the editor's grid shows the exact lines the overlays snap to.

items.title: The FPS counter stays on
items.text: On some PCs the counter switched between the frame rate and "waiting for the game" every moment. Windows hands over the game's frames in batches, and the counter took a late batch for a stopped game. It now asks for the frames twice a second and only says it's waiting after three seconds without any.

items.title: The meter steps aside in game windows again
items.text: The meter stays over the game's windows only while it shows your group, or for a few minutes after a boss fight while that fight is still on it (for the death screen and the page to commend players). Reset it, or let it fold to its bar, and it steps aside in the skill window and the rest as before.

items.title: Smooth scrolling through your fights
items.text: Ranks and pictures coming in no longer redraw the whole list while you scroll, the pictures are read at the size they're shown, and the list shows the newest 60 fights first with a button for older ones.

items.title: Tips and windows stay above the meter
items.text: Once a second every overlay goes back to the front so the game can't cover it, and that also put the meter over its own button tips, over a player's card and over the panels you open from it. These now go back to the front after the overlays.

items.title: Overlays on your second screen
items.text: With two screens, the overlay editor lets you pick the one the overlays go on. Click Screen 2 and every overlay moves there, in the same spot relative to that screen's corners, and the editor goes along to arrange them. They still show while the game is in front, also when the game is on the other screen. The Atreia button stays over the game.
items.example: The game on your main screen, the meter, the timers and the world bosses on the screen beside it.

items.title: The overlay editor
items.text: One key (Ctrl+Alt+V unless you changed it), or the first button of the overlay menu, opens the overlay editor over the game. Every overlay is a tile: click it to switch it on or off. While the editor is open each overlay shows where it sits on a faint grid, so you see how it will look: drag it, size it at its corners. An overlay's key is on its tile: click the key and press new ones. Size and opacity for all of them, the Atreia button and Alt + drag are there too. Done locks everything in place.
items.example: Press Ctrl+Alt+V, switch on Timers and World bosses, drag them under the minimap, set the opacity to 70 % and press Done.

items.title: Your group stays when you join
items.text: Rooms are joined in the game's group finder, which counts as a game window, so the meter showed your group and vanished a moment later. While you're in a group the meter now stays, also over the game's windows. Switch off Show my group in Settings if you'd rather it stepped aside.

items.title: Leaving a group clears it
items.text: Leave the room, get taken out of it, or have it close after the run: the group goes from the meter and it's back to how it was. Before, the old group stayed until you joined another.

items.title: The meter stays when you die and on the commend page
items.text: For three minutes after your last fight the meter stays on screen over the death screen and the page to commend players, right when you want to look at the fight.

items.title: Hotkeys keep your settings
items.text: The Skill Assist key hides what of it is on screen and brings back exactly that: it no longer turns the buffs on when you had them off. The key for all overlays brings back exactly what it hid, also after a restart.

items.title: Locked overlays stay where they are
items.text: Alt is the game's own key for the cursor, so with Alt + drag on, an overlay came along when you clicked in the game with Alt held. Alt + drag is off now; place overlays in the editor, or switch it on there if you want it.

items.title: See-through windows over the game
items.text: The panels you open from the meter (Characters, Journey, Legion …), a player's card and the overlay menu are see-through like the meter, at your overlays' opacity, with no light line along the top.

items.title: The Atreia button opens the menu
items.text: A click on the Atreia button over the game opens the overlay menu again, also while you're placing overlays, and a drag moves it. In the menu, click an overlay's key to change it.

items.title: Big changes read as times as much
items.text: Against a week when you barely played, a rise shows as ↗ 28× instead of ↗ 2703 %.

items.title: Your group, the moment you join it
items.text: Join a party or go into a dungeon with one (exploration, Conquest, Ludra …) and the meter opens Find a player with your group by itself, each member with their class, server and Combat Power, looked up for you in the background. A click shows their card at once. It never takes the keyboard from the game, and it folds away when a boss fight starts. The meter also stays up in dungeons and while you're in a group, so you can look someone up any time. Both are on by default and can be switched off in Settings, under the meter.
items.example: Your exploration group fills up: the meter shows Lunessa 171,204, Korrin 189,455 and Valtheris 182,730 before you've even entered.

items.title: Smoother overlays
items.text: The overlays fade in when they come up, their bars glide to new values instead of jumping, and the moments that matter glow briefly: a season mission done, an event going live, a skill coming off cooldown, a Pure or Radiant resource gathered. Upcoming events on the timers overlay have a thin bar that fills as they come closer.

items.title: Network, hotkeys, gathering and cooldowns redone
items.text: The network overlay is a small pill now: your ping, a graph of the last minute and a word for how it's going; hold Alt over it for every line. The hotkey overlay is a two-column cheat sheet that shows while you hold Ctrl+Alt. Gathering shows one bar per resource split into its grades, with the counts on one line. Cooldown bars are softer, with a gold fill while they run and a green fade when ready. The overlay menu is grouped into Combat, World, Tools and System, with icons and a tip on each overlay. The meter's colour legend hides itself after your first five sessions. The small network overlay and the hotkeys peek can be switched off on the Overlays page.

items.title: Hold Alt and drag any overlay
items.text: Every overlay now moves with the mouse in the game: hold Alt (the game shows the cursor), the overlay under it glows gold, and you drag it where you want it. Let go of Alt and your clicks go to the game again. The meter moves the same way unless you locked it with its padlock. "Move overlays" (Ctrl+Alt+V) still unlocks them all at once, with the handles to size them. You can switch Alt + drag off on the Overlays page.
items.example: The loot overlay covers your quest list: hold Alt, drag it to the corner, let go.

items.title: An FPS counter
items.text: Turn on the FPS counter in the overlay menu (or on the Overlays page): the game's frames per second, green from 60, amber from 30, red below, with the 1% low under it. It reads Windows' own frame timing, the way the Xbox Game Bar does, and never touches the game. Windows has to allow this once: the counter shows an Allow button that adds you to Windows' "Performance Log Users" group (Windows asks first), then sign out of Windows and in again.

items.title: A smaller overlay button you can move
items.text: The Atreia button at the top of the screen is now a small square with the emblem, and it shows the keys of Move overlays (the overlay editor) on it. Click it for the overlay menu as before, or drag it anywhere you like: it stays where you leave it.

items.title: Everything from the meter
items.text: A new button on the meter's bar opens a launcher with a tile for each tool: Characters, CP calculator, Journey, Legion, Items, Gathering, Season missions, Timers, Map and History. A tile opens that page right over the game, in a panel that looks like the meter, so you never have to leave the game for the app. Drag it by its top, size it at its edges, close it with Esc; it comes back where you left it. Pages that belong together are tabs of one panel.
items.example: Mid-dungeon you want your CP upgrades: open the launcher, click CP calculator, check them, press Esc and carry on.

items.title: Overlay switches on the launcher
items.text: Items, Gathering, Season missions, Timers and Map have their overlay's switch right on their tile, and the tile itself opens the numbers behind it: your drops and drop rates, everything you gathered, or the season missions of the character you're on, where you pick which ones the overlay shows.

items.title: The overlays look like the meter
items.text: The network, hotkey, world boss, crafting, training dummy, season missions and gathering overlays now share the meter's look: its background and soft edge, round corners and a small gold heading. The network overlay says at a glance whether your connection is all good, unsteady or in trouble, and the hotkey overlay shows its keys as keycaps. The meter's Tools and … menus have icons, and Characters there now opens over the game.

items.title: Siege and boss timers on the new days
items.text: The timetable follows the game's new schedule: the Artifact Siege and the Artifact bosses (the Executors) now run only on Thursday and Saturday (no more Monday), and Argo, the Spirit King spawns every day at 10:30 and 22:30 on your server's clock. The timers, the in-game timetable and the field boss list all show the new times. The timetable also comes from atreia.app now, so the next change shows up without an update.
items.example: Monday evening on NA East: the timetable no longer counts down to a siege that isn't coming. It shows the next one, Thursday at 21:00, with the Executors at 21:30, and Argo at 22:30 tonight.

items.title: Ludra's mechanics where they really land
items.text: The replay draws a boss's attacks in their real shape: circles, rings, cones, lines and crosses, pointing the way the boss faces. For Abyssal Forge: Ludra, the sizes come from 31 recorded Eternal Ludra pulls and the other bosses of the run. Most of Ludra's dangerous attacks come from the things she leaves on the floor, like the pools and the Airborne zones, not from Ludra herself. The replay now shows those in violet for as long as they stay, and their hits on your group count. The map is also the right way up now, with north on top like the game's map. Before, it was upside down.
items.example: You replay a wipe: the violet pool next to your Cleric was there for 12 seconds, and the Airborne zone that killed her lit up a second before she died.

items.title: Ludra's attacks timed from the first pull
items.text: The cast bar knows which of Ludra's attacks hit an area and how long after the cast the hit lands, from your very first pull. Before, the meter had to see each attack a few times first.
items.example: First Ludra of the week: the bar marks her attack as an area and counts down to the hit, 1.5 s after the cast ends.

items.title: Altgard and Verteron maps line up with the land
items.text: The Altgard map picture was drawn 1.8 % too small, so the further you were from the middle, the further off it was: up to 80 m at the western edge. Verteron's picture sat about 60 m off. Both are now refitted from about 10,000 position checks from 13 PCs. Every PC reads the minimap a little off in its own way, depending on its screen setup, so the refit measures each PC's own offset separately instead of mistaking it for the map's. Once a PC's own offset is taken off, the Altgard map is now within 1 to 4 m everywhere players walked. The app also learns your offset separately for each window size, so switching resolution no longer mixes them up. From this version, the map checks include your game window's size and the minimap's zoom. That lets the next refit correct each resolution from the first second, and the app asks you once to accept the updated privacy note that says so. The Abyss maps were already close. Eltnen, Morheim and Middle Reshanta get the same fix once enough checks come in.

items.title: Your group, one click each
items.text: Open Find a player while you're in a group and the other players of your group are listed under the box, with their class and server. Click one to see their card, Combat Power, Item Level and best parse, without typing the name. The list keeps up while it's open: players who join show up and players who leave go, within a couple of seconds. Clear the box to get the list back.
items.example: Your Nightmare group has a Cleric you don't know: open Find a player, click Lunessa, and her card comes up.

items.title: The other party in a raid, too
items.text: In a fight with two parties together, like Ludra, the game only tells you who is in your own party. Under your group, Find a player now also lists the players fighting with you: everyone who hit the same monsters as your group or healed it in the last 10 minutes, most damage first. In a raid that is the other party; at an open-world boss it can include strangers at the same boss. Each one is a click away from their card.
items.example: At Ludra, open Find a player: your three party members, then under Fighting with you the four players of the other party.

items.title: Daevanion boards node by node
items.text: A player's page has a Daevanion tab: pick a board and see it the way the game draws it, every node in its place, the open ones lit. Point at a node to see what it gives, and under the board you see everything the open nodes add up to, stats and skill levels. On the Overview, a click on a board's line opens it. This works for every character, with or without the app.
items.example: You open a Templar's page, click Nezekan: 48 of 60 nodes lit, and under it Critical Hit +120, Max HP +1,400 and Shield Bash Lv. +2 from the open nodes.

items.title: The welcome window's buttons on smaller screens
items.text: On a laptop or another smaller screen, the welcome window you see the first time was taller than the screen, so its Back and Next buttons were out of sight and you could only close it. Now the privacy text scrolls in its own box and the buttons always stay at the bottom of the window.

items.title: A player's page is up to date when you open it
items.text: Opening a player's page shows what the website has right away, then reads the character's game page again when the website's copy is more than 10 minutes old, the same as pressing refresh. Combat Power and Item Level always show the newest numbers the website has, for example from that player's last login with the app. Before, a copy up to two days old could show last week's numbers.
items.example: You open YIELD's page: it shows 183,235 Combat Power and Item Level 2,914 from this evening's login, not the 180,972 from two days ago.

items.title: Exact combat stats, or none
items.text: The Stats tab of a player's page shows Attack, Accuracy, Critical Hit, HP, MP, Defense, Evasion and Critical Hit Resist with the exact numbers of the game's own character window, and when they were sent. These come from that player's own Atreia App, because the game sends them to nobody else. The rough totals from the character page are gone, since they never matched the game. A player without the app now gets a note saying their stats show once they use Atreia App, instead of numbers that were wrong.
items.example: You look up Mirelle, who plays with the app: Attack 3,254, Defense 17,314, HP 31,402, the same as in her own window 12 minutes ago.

items.title: Your stats go with your Genus and pets
items.text: While you're signed in, your character's combat stats are shared along with your Genus Insight and pets, so other app users who look you up see your real numbers. They go a minute after a login, and again at most every few minutes when they change (buffs included). The switch in the Atreia account window is now called "Show my Genus Insight, pets and combat stats", and switching it off deletes what was sent.

items.title: Your Hidden Cube keys, and no cube alerts without one
items.text: The Cube finder shows how many Hidden Cube keys your character has in the bag, and how many more are in storage. The meter's cube line and the cube note show it too. A character with no key in the bag now gets no cube alerts (no note, no sounds, no meter line, no map popping up), so you're not sent to cubes you can't open; the cubes still show on the map. This is on for everyone now, and you can switch it off in the Cube finder (Only when I carry a key).
items.example: On your alt with no keys the cube sounds stay quiet; on your main the note reads "Hidden Cube nearby · 42 m · 3 keys".

items.title: Your meter's columns in the fight report
items.text: The columns you picked for the meter in its look settings (crit, back, front, perfect, double, parried, hits, nDPS and Given) now also show in a fight's report from the History: on the Damage tab's player list, and on the line above the skills of the player you click. The report gets wider to fit them.
items.example: With Crit and Back ticked, a Ludra report from yesterday shows each player's crit and back attack share next to their accuracy.

items.title: Attack, defense, accuracy and crit in a character's stats
items.text: A character's Stats tab now starts with their combat stats: Attack, Accuracy, Critical Hit, Penetration and the damage boosts, then Defense, HP, Block, Evasion and Critical Hit Resist. They are added up from the gear, Daevanion, titles and attributes on the game's character page; the game's base stats aren't on that page, so they aren't included. Point at an attribute to see what it gives.
items.example: Look up Dranna: the Stats tab shows her Attack and Critical Hit at the top, with Might, Justice and the other attributes under them.

items.title: Find a player in your fights
items.text: The History has a search box: type part of a name and it shows everyone with it in the name who was in your fights, with how many fights and when last. The tabs below then list only the fights with them; click a name to look for that player alone. Fights saved before this update are read for their players once, in the background, the first time you open the History.
items.example: Type "kash": Kashlyn shows up in 14 of your fights, last on Nov 8, and the Boss fights tab lists those 14.

items.title: The account window is readable
items.text: In the Atreia account window, the two switches (sending your legion's member list, showing your Genus Insight and pets) were cut off at the edge and drawn in a dim grey. Their text wraps now, in the normal text colour.
items.example: Open your account from the menu: both switches read in full.

items.title: New boss pictures without a restart
items.text: When new boss pictures come out, the app uses them as soon as they have downloaded in the background, and the Fights page shows them right away. Before, they only showed after restarting the app twice.
items.example: Zikel's Apparition gets its picture while the app is open.

versions.headline: Atreia App moves into its own name: fits every screen, installs and updates from atreia.app

items.title: Every window fits your screen
items.text: Every window and overlay now fits the screen it opens on, from 1280 × 720 to 4K and ultrawide, also with Windows' display scaling, and again when you change your screens. Settings, the session manager and the character roster were too big for small screens before. An overlay left on a screen that is gone comes back onto one you have; otherwise overlays stay where you put them.
items.example: At 1280 × 720 Settings opens whole, with its buttons at the bottom on the screen.

items.title: Installs under its own name, in a tidy folder
items.text: The app now installs in %LOCALAPPDATA%\AtreiaApp as AtreiaApp.exe, and keeps your settings, characters and history in %APPDATA%\AtreiaApp. Both folders were still called A2HMeter. On its first start it moves your data over by itself and removes the old install, its shortcuts included. The install folder is tidy now: the app, its assets, the .NET runtime in a folder of its own and the licenses, instead of hundreds of loose files and 13 language folders that were not the app's languages.
items.example: Your pinned taskbar icon and "Start with Windows" keep working and now start the new install.

items.title: Updates come from atreia.app
items.text: The installer and the updates are on atreia.app now, together with these notes. If your app still installs in A2HMeter, it can't update itself any more: download the installer from atreia.app once, and it takes everything over.
items.example: atreia.app/download/Atreia-App-Setup.exe

items.title: The game's pictures, downloaded once
items.text: The game's icons and maps (items, skills, pets, bosses, wings, classes) come as one download of about 40 MB on the first start, with the progress shown, instead of inside the app. They are kept on your PC; a newer set comes by itself in the background.
items.example: First start: a small window shows "12 of 40 MB", then the meter opens with every icon.

items.title: Monsters named right after a dungeon
items.text: After a dungeon, ordinary monsters in the open world could be named after its boss on the meter: Kerubars as Mutated Gerod, Kerubiel as Zikel's Apparition. The game gives a boss's number to the next monster once the boss is gone, and the meter kept the boss's name for it. Now each monster keeps its own name.
items.example: Killing Kerubars on the beach after Blades Hideout: the meter's title names the fight right, not Mutated Gerod.

items.title: Bosses show their own picture
items.text: Boss fights without a picture of their boss showed your class icon in the history. Field bosses now show their portraits, Nightmare and Conquest bosses the picture of their boss, and Eternal Ludra has one. A boss without any picture shows its first letter.
items.example: Rahu and Ketu show "R" and "K" instead of your class icon.

items.title: Combat Power on every character
items.text: The characters list said "Level 45" for every character at the top. It now shows each character's Combat Power, as last seen when it logged in, else its Item Level.
items.example: "124.1K CP · Fafnir · seen 1 m ago"

versions.headline: Eternal Ludra: its attacks named in the callouts, and no stagger checks the game broke by itself

items.title: Ludra's attacks named
items.text: The game calls most of Eternal Ludra's attacks just "Attack". The ones with a clear effect now carry a name in the callouts and the fight report: Hits everyone, Stun, Knockdown, Airborne, Watch, and Despairing Aura / Chaos Aura. Purple Bolt, Ludra's Trial, Ure's Area and Supply Eldritch Energy keep the game's own names.
items.example: At 70 % the line reads "Hits everyone in 4 s" instead of "Attack in 4 s".

items.title: Ludra's bar is no stagger check
items.text: Eternal Ludra's stagger bar never goes down from hits; the game breaks it by itself after Purple Bolt and after Ludra's Trial. The meter showed those as checks of three minutes that nobody had a part in. A bar that broke or ended with next to nothing taken off is no check any more. Abyssal Wings Ketu's checks are unchanged: its bar does go down from your hits.
items.example: After a Ludra pull the Stagger view shows no checks instead of a three-minute "broken" one.

versions.headline: All your characters, a meter that grows with the players, and PvP in the Abyss

items.title: Every character of your server on the page
items.text: A character made on another server and moved, or on a server that was merged, came with its old server, and the page left it out. The server you log in on now counts for every character on your list. Log in once to bring them back.
items.example: Five characters on Beritra: all five show, whichever one you log in with.

items.title: The meter grows with the players, up to ten lines
items.text: The meter's lines take as much room as there are players, up to ten, and shrink back when they go. A height you dragged is now the most it takes, so it no longer opens as a tall empty box. It also no longer opens by itself with nothing to show.
items.example: Three players: three lines. Twelve in a siege: ten lines, the best on top.

items.title: PvP counted in the Abyss and the open world
items.text: When you hit another player or one hits you, the fight is counted and shown wherever you are, the Abyss too, without switching on the open world.
items.example: A fight against the other side in Lower Reshanta shows your damage and theirs.

versions.headline: Skill cooldowns that keep running while your buffs tick

items.title: Buffs and channels no longer restart their cooldown
items.text: Some skills keep sending hits after you use them: Flame Blessing's flames while the blessing is on, a channel's hits, an aura's or a mantra's pulses. The Skill Assist took each one for a new use, so Flame Blessing showed about 1 second the whole time and other buffs showed a few seconds more than the game. Now only the use starts the cooldown, and short lengths learnt from those hits are thrown away.
items.example: Flame Blessing used: 60 s counts down from the cast, whatever its flames do meanwhile.

versions.headline: Cooldowns no longer reset when a party member buffs you, and cube alerts only with a key

items.title: Cooldowns no longer reset at every buff
items.text: Since 1.20.61 a buff from a party member of another class (a Chanter's or Cleric's) could make the Skill Assist think you had switched class, and every cooldown jumped back to ready. Buffs no longer touch your cooldowns; only your own skills switch the class.
items.example: A Chanter buffs your Ranger in the middle of a fight: your cooldowns keep counting down.

items.title: Cube alerts only when you carry a key
items.text: A new switch on the Cube finder page: the note, the sounds, the meter's line and the map coming up only while your character has a Hidden Cube key in its bag. The cube still shows on the map.
items.example: Out of keys, you farm in peace; pick one up and the next cube calls you again.

versions.headline: Abyss Corridors on the Characters page, and only your server

items.title: Abyss Corridors on the Characters page
items.text: A new column shows how many Abyss Corridors each character still has to enter since the last Artifact Siege. The game hands them out when a character first enters the Abyss after the siege; a character that has not been there yet shows the number your other character got, marked with ~.
items.example: Your side holds two artifacts: Draegor shows 1 after one corridor, Nyxelle shows ~2 until she enters the Abyss.

items.title: Only the server you play on
items.text: Characters from a server you no longer play on no longer show on the Characters page and the home page. It follows the server of the character you are logged in with, or the one you played last.

versions.headline: Each class its own Skill Assist, a compass that fades, one clean font

items.title: The right class's skills on every character
items.text: After switching characters, the Skill Assist could still list the skills of the class you played before until the game sent a cooldown. It now follows your character's class from the login, and from the first skill you use if the app was started later.
items.example: You log out of your Assassin and into your Ranger: the other skills listed are the Ranger's right away.

items.title: Each class keeps its own layout and presets
items.text: Every class now has its own look (bars or squares, size, see-through), its own places and its own three presets, and the app switches to them by itself when you play that class. You can also pick the class by hand, and copy another class's layout onto this one: its bars or squares go to the same spots, first skill of the bar to first skill of the bar.
items.example: Your Templar's cooldowns sit just how you like them: on your Cleric, pick Copy the layout of Templar and they line up the same way.

items.title: The compass only for a moment
items.text: A new switch next to Compass on the Interactive map page: the N, NE, E ... letters around the map show for 3 seconds when it comes up, zooms, changes map or your mouse rests on it, then fade, so they don't sit over the map the whole time. The Compass switch still turns them off completely.
items.example: The map pops up for a Hidden Cube: the letters show you which way is north, then get out of the way.

items.title: One clean font everywhere
items.text: Titles, character names and the charts now use the same font as the buttons and the rest of the app, instead of the old decorative capitals and a second font in the charts.

versions.headline: Just the frames on the Black Cloud shop, and updates straight to the newest

items.title: Only the frames on the shop, no pop-up
items.text: The pop-up at the top of the screen is gone: the pets you still need are just framed on the shop's page, with their genus and level. A pet you buy loses its frame at once and isn't marked again until the merchant's offers renew, and finished pets are never marked.
items.example: You buy Furious Feruk: its frame goes away right there, and the next time you open the shop this hour it stays unmarked.

items.title: Frames that stayed when you clicked
items.text: Clicking a card opened the purchase window, but the frame stayed where the card had been. Now any click or key takes the frames away at once, and they come back only on cards that are still there once the screen has settled.
items.example: Click Furious Feruk, the purchase window opens: no frame floating over it. Cancel it, and the frame is back on the card.

items.title: The genera named as the game names them
items.text: Cogni, Fera, Natura, Varian and Special, as in the game (in your game's language), on the Pets page, the shop frames, the map note and the pet route.

items.title: Straight to the newest version
items.text: An update now always goes to the newest version, in one restart, however many you skipped. One that was downloaded earlier isn't put in on its own any more when a newer one is out, and "What's new" lists every change from all the versions you missed.
items.example: You were on 1.20.55: one update takes you to the newest, and What's new shows 1.20.56 to today in one list.

versions.headline: The Black Cloud pop-up redone, its pets marked on the shop, and pet alerts your way

items.title: A clearer pop-up, and the card marked on the shop
items.text: The pop-up when the Black Cloud Merchant sells a pet you still need is redone: each pet's picture in a ring of its genus's colour, its genus (Cognia, Fera, Natura, Varia, Specia), where it comes from, how far your character has it and the price. On the shop's page the pet's card gets a frame in the same colour, with its genus and level on top, so you don't have to look for it. The card is found in the game window's own picture; nothing is read from the game.
items.example: You open the shop on your alt: "Urugugu Brawler, Cognia, level 1 of 3, 90,000 Kinah", and its card on the page lights up blue.

items.title: No pop-up for pets you've finished
items.text: A pet the character already has at the top level never brings the pop-up or the renewal note any more. Only what that character still needs is shown.
items.example: White Bunny is maxed on your main: opening the shop there stays quiet about it, on your alt it still tells you.

items.title: Pick which genera you get alerts for
items.text: A new Pet alerts card on the Pets page: tick the genera you care about. The Black Cloud pop-up, its renewal note and the map below follow it.
items.example: You only farm Cognia and Natura: untick the others and the merchant's Fera pets stop popping up.

items.title: The map comes up when a pet you need is near
items.text: Switch it on in Pet alerts and pick how near (100 m to 1 km). When your character comes that close to a monster of a pet you still need, of the genera you picked, the interactive map comes up over the game with a note of which pet and how far, like it does for a Hidden Cube. It goes again 10 seconds after none is that near, and works with the map switched off.
items.example: Within 300 m of a Vivel spawn you still need: the map pops up with "Fera · Vivel nearby · 240 m".

versions.headline: An overlay menu in the game, hotkeys your way, and a sharper stagger split

items.title: An overlay menu at the top of the game's screen
items.text: A small Atreia button now sits at the top of the screen while you play. Click it for every overlay with its switch and its hotkey, and to move or hide them all, change the hotkeys or open the app, without leaving the game. If it is in the way, move it with the other overlays (Move overlays), or switch it off on the Overlays page.
items.example: Halfway through a dungeon you want the loot overlay but forgot its key: show the cursor, click Atreia, click Loot.

items.title: Hotkeys your way, and you can see the ones that don't work
items.text: F keys, the number pad and Insert, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down now work on their own, without Ctrl or Alt. A hotkey another program already uses (graphics drivers and recording tools like to take Ctrl+Alt keys) is shown in red in the hotkey overlay and in Settings > Hotkeys, with what to do about it. Giving a combination another hotkey had moves it over instead of quietly breaking one of them, and "Back to the default keys" sets them all back. Each press now says at the top of the screen what it switched. Your keys are kept in your own settings, so an update never changes them.
items.example: Ctrl+Alt+C did nothing because your graphics driver had it. The hotkey list shows it in red, and you give the Boss fight overlay F7 instead.

items.title: No addresses on the network overlay
items.text: The Server line showed the game server's address and the Local network line your router's. Neither is shown any more, so nothing on stream gives an address away: the Server line just says you're connected.

items.title: The stagger split checked on 211 boss fights
items.text: A skill takes the same off the stagger bar at every level, but the game gives each level its own id, so the app used to miss many skills and had to guess. It now knows each skill's amount at any level, for all eight classes, checked on 211 real boss fights against 21 bosses with a stagger bar (Krao Cave, Draupnir, Urugugu Canyon, Vakron Sky Island, Ferocious Horn Den, Shattered Arkanis, Nightmare and more). 94% of all the stagger in those fights now matches the exact skill that did it, up from about 70%.

items.title: Ludra: Rahu's long cast is no failed check
items.text: Isolation Specialist Rahu in Abyssal Forge: Ludra has a 15 second cast during which the bar can't be staggered at all. The app showed it as a check your group failed with nothing taken off. It doesn't any more; Rahu's real checks are still shown.
items.example: Two minutes in, Rahu starts the long cast with a full bar. Before, that read "Failed, 0 of 4,500". Now it isn't listed as a check.

versions.headline: A sharper stagger split, and update notes

items.title: Who took what off the bar, far more precisely
items.text: A skill takes the same off the stagger bar at every level, but the game gives each level its own id, so the app used to miss many skills and had to guess. It now knows each skill's amount at any level, for all eight classes, worked out from real boss fights.
items.example: Judgment, Chain of Torment, the Spiritmaster's spirits: all counted by what they really take off, instead of the nearest hit.

items.title: No phantom 240 when Berk's bar changes size
items.text: When a boss's stagger bar switches size (Berk goes from 720 to 480), the difference was counted as stagger nobody did. It isn't any more. Only the Gladiator's and Assassin's hits are marked as boosted now, as only they have the stagger buff.

items.title: What's new, right in the update prompt
items.text: When a new version is ready, open "What's new" under the prompt to read every change since the version you have, with examples. After the update the app shows them once, so nothing slips by.
items.example: You skipped a few days. The prompt lists everything since your version, newest first, so you can read it all in one place.

versions.headline: Stagger on the meter, and accuracy in reports

items.title: A Stagger button next to Group
items.text: Click Stagger on the meter and the lines make room for the boss's stagger check: the mechanic, the time left, and exactly how much each player took off the bar, with the skills they used. Players who took nothing off show a red 0. Click Group (or any other scope) to get the lines back.
items.example: Berk starts Extinction for Eternity. The meter shows 2.8 s left, 336 to go, and Kaivhan 50, Nyxelle 45, Seraphyne 35, Draegor 14, Lumiael 0.

items.title: Earlier checks one click away
items.text: Under the current check, every earlier check of the same boss sits as a small chip: green with the time it broke in, red with what was left. Click one to look at it again; a new check takes over as soon as it starts.
items.example: Checks: 1 ✗ 222 left · 2 ✓ 6.4 s · 3 ✗ 66 left

items.title: A new Stagger tab
items.text: The boss's stagger bar over the whole fight. Each check is a band from the cast that starts it to the end of that cast: green when the bar broke in time, red when it didn't, with what was left. Hover anywhere for the bar's exact value. Click a check, or drag across any stretch, to see who took how much off it.
items.example: Drag from 0:30 to 0:41 and you see that Draegor took 49 off the bar in those eleven seconds and Lumiael none.

items.title: Accuracy on the Damage tab
items.text: Every skill, every player and the total now have an Accuracy figure. Against a boss, low accuracy doesn't show as a miss: the boss parries or blocks, and the hit lands for a third to half of its damage. Accuracy is the share of your hits that landed in full (a dodged attack counts as a miss too).
items.example: Seraphyne 97.7%: about 2 hits in every 100 were parried or blocked.

items.title: Only the real bosses in the fights list
items.text: In a dungeon whose bosses the app knows, side fights like Urugugu Patrol and Urugugu Shaman are no longer listed, and they no longer count in the day's kills and wipes or in your personal bests. They are still in the report of the whole run.
items.example: Urugugu Canyon now lists Guardian Captain Raur, Judge Urahum and Divine Auldor, and nothing else.

versions.headline: Stagger checks: who really used theirs

items.title: Every stagger check, player by player
items.text: The app finds each stagger check of a boss (the bar fills when a mechanic starts and has to break before the cast ends) and works out exactly how much each player took off it. The Assassin's and Gladiator's stagger buff is counted: those hits take half as much again.
items.example: Wave of Death, not broken: 245 of 736 left. Kaivhan 195, Seraphyne 146, Draegor 65, Lumiael 55, Nyxelle 30.

items.title: Hover a skill to see each hit
items.text: Every player's line has the icons of the skills that took something off the bar. Hover one for what each hit did, which ones had the stagger buff, and when they landed. Skills that hit the boss but took nothing off show faded, so "I used mine" can be checked.
items.example: Shadowstrike: 85 off the bar in 7 hits. Each hit 4 × 10, 3 × 15 (3 with a stagger buff).

versions.headline: CP calculator: the game's own level tables

items.title: Skill and Stigma levels as the game counts them
items.text: Skills and Stigmas now go up by the game's own tables, so the CP of each next level is what you'll actually get. Daevanion steps stay within the points the game lets you spend.
items.example: The suggested skill order is now levels 8, 12, 16 and 20: the levels where a skill gains the most CP.

versions.headline: Boss timers that know the pattern

items.title: Next casts from the boss's pattern
items.text: The boss timers now learn when a cast comes from what happened before it: the attack before, the boss's health and the time into the fight. Every version of a boss counts, and so do the fights on your own PC. Hover a timer to see what it was learned from.
items.example: Flame Breath 12 s, Enrage 0:48, right over your meter's lines.

items.title: No rank pop-up over the game
items.text: After an upload your rank shows in History and on the fight's page, but no longer pops up over the game in the middle of the next pull.

items.title: The shop's clock on the pet list
items.text: The Black Cloud Merchants' pet list shows when the shop changes next, and a reminder comes every hour, so a pet you still need never goes by unseen.
items.example: Black Cloud Merchants · Ashveil: ticked pets on offer. Swift Lugi, 1,200,000 Kinah.

items.title: Cheapest upgrades first, in your build's order
items.text: The next steps are sorted by CP for the Kinah they cost, and Stigmas and skills follow your class build's order. Every Stigma or skill step says whether it's part of your build.

items.title: A wipe never leaks into the next pull
items.text: The next attempt starts when the boss is pulled again, not on a stray hit after the wipe. Each attempt is saved in History the moment it ends, killed or wiped.

items.title: Bursts, drops and deaths
items.text: The fight report points out the fight's best and worst moments: where the group's damage peaked, where it dropped and why (the boss staggered, the boss casting, a death). Deaths also show on the meter, after the player's name.
items.example: 0:14 to 0:20: burst, 1.9× the usual while the boss was staggered. Lumiael ☠ 1:12.

items.title: A world boss page with faces
items.text: Every region's field bosses on one page, at the game's times to the minute, each with its portrait, here and on the overlay.
items.example: Sharp Shylok, Watcher Kaira, Advisor Resana... and when each one is up next.

items.title: OBS widgets with links that keep working
items.text: The Streaming page has three widgets for OBS: the meter, your character card and the boss bar. Each has its own link to paste as a browser source, and the link stays the same after a restart.

versions.headline: Ranks, smoother play and Kinah-smart upgrades

items.title: Your rank on every uploaded boss
items.text: Upload a boss fight and History shows where your DPS ranks among everyone's fights on that boss.
items.example: Talisra of the Void, 96: better than 96% of the uploaded fights.

items.title: Upgrades priced at your server's market
items.text: Every suggested step shows what it costs at your own server's market prices, so "best value" means best value for you.

items.title: Less lag while you play
items.text: The app now takes one picture of the game window for both the menu check and the minimap, and reads the minimap less often. A new Status page shows what the app is doing, with a report you can copy when asking for help.

items.title: No more wrong cube arrow
items.text: The beam over a Hidden Cube and the arrow at the screen's edge are gone for now: the camera direction they relied on was never right. The distance on the meter and the map are unchanged.

items.title: Characters as a table again
items.text: Each character is one line of a table with its counters in small boxes, and the totals sit in one low strip on top. A narrow window shows a character's whole line when you hover it.

items.title: Send your legion's member list to the website
items.text: From the Legion page, send the member list to atreia.app in one click. The site tells you if it can't take it (only a verified member, or a leader of a following server, may send it).

items.title: Names with accents no longer break the list
items.text: One accented name used to throw the whole member list off. Every member now shows on the legion's own server.

versions.headline: A cleaner look everywhere

items.title: Your last 7 days at a glance
items.text: History opens on a board of your last week: each fight against your best on that boss, and your personal bests as cards.

items.title: Characters, tools and maps in the new look
items.text: Clearer titles, controls together on one bar, sections under a gold line. Characters shows when your Odyle energy will be full.
items.example: Odyle energy 520 / 840: full in ~4 d.

items.title: Boss health lives on the meter
items.text: The boss's health is now the boss line over the meter's lines, so the separate boss health overlay is gone. Find a player has its own button on the meter.

versions.headline: Your legion, and OBS widgets

items.title: A Legion page
items.text: Your legion's members, read from the game when you log in, with search and sorting, and your legion on Discord through the Atreia bot.
items.example: Dawnbreakers: 24 members, average combat power 196.0K.

items.title: Three OBS widgets
items.text: The meter, your character card and the boss bar, each with its own link for OBS.
